meta.provenanceNote: Compiled from public API pricing archives, Epoch AI open benchmark datasets, Stanford HAI AI Index, Artificial Analysis, and METR autonomous task evaluations.

gpqaExperts.label: PhD experts
gpqaExperts.note: Accuracy of PhD experts in the matching field on the GPQA Diamond question set (81.2–81.3%), from the GPQA paper. The paper notes this figure is skewed upward by how Diamond questions were selected, so it is a generous bar for humans. (Experts scored ~65% on the larger GPQA Extended set, which is not the set AI scores are reported on.)

costDecaySeries.title: Price of Expert-Level AI per 1 Million Blended Tokens (USD)
costDecaySeries.subtitle: Each point is a new record-low list price for an AI model that scores at or above PhD experts (~81%) on GPQA Diamond PhD-level science questions.
costDecaySeries.humanAnalogy: A million tokens is roughly 750,000 words of AI reading and writing. The cheapest AI that beats PhD experts on these science questions fell from $1.93 to $0.20 per million tokens in 17 months.
costDecaySeries.caveat: All of these are reasoning models, which spend extra 'thinking' tokens before answering, so the real cost per question is higher than the per-token price. Open-weights models are excluded because their price depends on the host.

points.label: o4-mini (high)
points.note: First verified model priced under $2 per million tokens to score above PhD experts on GPQA Diamond (81.4%, high reasoning).

points.label: Gemini 2.5 Flash
points.note: General release scores 82.8% on GPQA Diamond at less than half o4-mini's price.

points.label: GPT-5 mini
points.note: 82.3% on GPQA Diamond (high reasoning, no tools).

points.label: GPT-6 Luna
points.note: Scores ~90% on GPQA Diamond in Epoch AI's independent evaluation (OpenRouter measured 87.4%); OpenAI has not published a vendor score.

capabilityBenchmarks.name: PhD-Level Science (GPQA Diamond)
capabilityBenchmarks.description: Graduate-level biology, chemistry and physics questions written by PhDs to be 'Google-proof'. Each point is a new record score at release (vendor-reported unless noted).

capabilityBenchmarks.name: Real Software Engineering (SWE-bench Verified)
capabilityBenchmarks.description: Share of 500 human-checked real GitHub issues from open-source Python projects resolved, verified by each project's own tests. Vendor-reported standard runs (no high-compute or parallel variants). Caveat: OpenAI stopped reporting this benchmark in Feb 2026, citing growing training-data contamination, so recent scores may overstate real-world ability.

taskHorizon.title: Autonomous Task Horizon (50% Reliability)
taskHorizon.subtitle: The length of software and research tasks—timed on skilled humans—that AI completes on its own at least half the time. METR measures a doubling roughly every 4 months since 2023 (about every 6 months over 2019–2026).
taskHorizon.caveat: Measures structured software, cyber and reasoning tasks with automatic scoring at 50% reliability—not open-ended judgment or physical work. METR says results above ~16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite, so this atlas only charts results whose 95% confidence interval stays under 16 hours (excluding, e.g., Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Mythos Preview).

frontierPrice.title: Price of the Best AI Each Year
frontierPrice.note: The top-scoring generally available model on GPQA Diamond at the end of each year (the same models as the 'Smarter' chart), at its published API list price per 1M tokens (3:1 input/output blend).
frontierPrice.trendNote: Top-model prices fell sharply through 2025, then rose again in 2026 as labs launched new premium tiers (e.g. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable). Within each tier, prices have since been cut.
frontierPrice.caveat: Anthropic and Google stopped publishing GPQA scores for their 2026 models (Anthropic calls the test saturated), so 2026 follows the highest reported score. On Epoch AI's independent capability index, Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra are statistically tied, at the same $8/$40 price. Claude 4.7+ models use a new tokenizer that produces ~30% more tokens for the same text.

frontierLabs.title: Each Lab's Best Model Per Year: List Price
frontierLabs.trendNote: Prices move up and down: they fell sharply through 2025, then rose in 2026 as labs launched new premium tiers.
frontierLabs.caveat: Each lab's most capable generally available model at the end of each year (Epoch Capabilities Index), at its published list price at that time. Google had no generally available, publicly priced flagship in 2023 (Gemini Pro was free in preview and priced per character). Gemini 1.5 Pro's post-October-2024 output price ($5.00) is reported by Google's pricing page but disputed in some coverage ($2.50). Gemini 4 Carbon is shown at its $4/$20 list price effective Dec 1, 2026 (introductory $2/$10 through Nov 30). Claude 4.7+ models use a tokenizer that produces ~30% more tokens for the same text.

flagshipModels.title: Flagship Models Over Time: Launch Price & Capability
flagshipModels.note: Top-tier, generally available models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google at launch list prices (standard context). ECI = Epoch Capabilities Index, an independent composite score (Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130, GPT-5 = 150). Limited-access previews (e.g. Claude Mythos) and xAI models (no verifiable GPQA scores) are excluded. 'Not reported' = the lab no longer publishes GPQA.

frontierMath.name: FrontierMath (Tiers 1–3, v2)
frontierMath.plainName: expert-written math problems that take professional mathematicians hours to days
frontierMath.description: Hundreds of unpublished, expert-written math problems from Epoch AI, ranging from advanced graduate level to research level. Scores are Epoch AI's own evaluations on the corrected v2 problem set (best score among models released that year).
frontierMath.caveat: OpenAI commissioned and funds FrontierMath and has seen most problem statements and many solutions; Epoch AI keeps a holdout set and runs all evaluations itself. v2 (June 2026) corrected errors in 42% of problems, so v1 and v2 scores are not comparable.

mathProgress.headline: From Olympiad gold to a computer-verified proof of the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis

milestones.title: Math Olympiad gold
milestones.text: 35 of 42 points, officially certified by IMO coordinators (Google DeepMind Gemini Deep Think). 2024: silver (28/42, AlphaProof).

milestones.title: Disproved an 80-year-old Erdős conjecture
milestones.text: An OpenAI model disproved Erdős's 1946 unit-distance conjecture; nine prominent mathematicians including Fields Medalist Tim Gowers assessed the proof.

milestones.title: Proof of the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis
milestones.text: Found by mathematician Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) working with Claude. The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative confirmed the statement and proof are correct in Lean; MIT independently rebuilt it. Not yet peer reviewed or understood by humans; the Clay Institute still lists it as open.

milestones.title: Proof that VP ≠ VNP (a major complexity question)
milestones.status: Claimed · not yet checked by humans
milestones.text: Written by an internal Claude model and posted by Anthropic with a Lean proof that compiles; Anthropic says no human has checked it. It does not settle P vs NP.

mathProgress.excludedNote: Several 2026 Math Olympiad perfect scores (42/42) were claimed by companies but not certified by the IMO, so they are not shown.

humanImpactTakeaways.title: Why Falling Prices Matter
humanImpactTakeaways.body: When AI that outscores PhD experts on science questions drops from $1.93 to $0.20 per million tokens in 17 months, expert-level help with tutoring, research reading, translation and software work becomes affordable for schools, clinics, small studios and independent researchers—not just large companies.

humanImpactTakeaways.title: Cheaper per Task vs. More Total Power
humanImpactTakeaways.body: Both are true at once: each unit of AI work keeps getting cheaper, while rapidly growing usage drives the large data center buildout mapped in our Data Centers tab (the Jevons paradox). Cheaper AI does not automatically mean less total energy or water.

humanImpactTakeaways.title: Honest Check: Benchmarks ≠ Real-World Perfection
humanImpactTakeaways.body: High scores on Olympiad math or PhD multiple-choice questions don't eliminate hallucinations, clinical liability, or social disruption. That's why this atlas tracks both breakthroughs and physical/community trade-offs side by side.
